questions.q: State the exact adjustment journal entry for closing stock when it is given as additional information outside the Trial Balance.
questions.a: Closing Stock A/c Dr. → To Trading A/c. A wrong answer like "Trading A/c Dr. To Closing Stock A/c" reveals the student confuses the direction: they think stock is an expense to be debited, not an asset to be recognised. Another common error "Closing Stock A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c" shows confusion with the adjusted purchases method (where stock appears inside Trial Balance).

questions.q: Explain why closing stock is credited to the Trading Account and not debited, even though stock is an asset.
questions.a: Closing stock is credited to Trading Account because it reduces the cost of goods sold (Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock). Since Trading Account is debited with opening stock and purchases, crediting closing stock completes the COGS calculation. A student who says "assets are always debited" misunderstands that here we are reversing the effect of purchases already debited; the asset recognition happens on the Balance Sheet side, not by debiting Trading Account.

questions.q: A trial balance shows Purchases ₹2,00,000 and Opening Stock ₹30,000. Additional information: Closing Stock ₹25,000. Calculate Cost of Goods Sold and show the Trading Account extract with correct figures.
questions.a: COGS = Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock = 30,000 + 2,00,000 - 25,000 = ₹2,05,000. Trading Account: Dr. side - Opening Stock ₹30,000, Purchases ₹2,00,000; Cr. side - Closing Stock ₹25,000, Gross Profit (balancing figure). If student gets ₹2,30,000 (forgetting to subtract closing stock) or ₹1,75,000 (subtracting from purchases only), they haven't grasped the three-component COGS formula.

questions.q: Compare the two methods of treating closing stock: (i) Additional information method vs (ii) Adjusted purchases method (where closing stock appears in Trial Balance). Identify two key differences in journal entries and final accounts presentation.
questions.a: Method (i): Entry: Closing Stock A/c Dr. To Trading A/c. Trading A/c shows Closing Stock on credit side; Balance Sheet shows Closing Stock as asset. Method (ii): Entry: Closing Stock A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c. Trading A/c shows Adjusted Purchases (Purchases - Closing Stock) on debit side; NO separate Closing Stock on credit side. Balance Sheet still shows Closing Stock as asset. A student missing that Trial Balance itself contains closing stock in method (ii) will pass wrong entries in exam.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "If closing stock is overvalued by ₹5,000 due to ignoring the lower of cost or NRV rule, both Gross Profit and Current Assets will be overstated by ₹5,000." Is this correct? Justify.
questions.a: Yes, correct. Overvalued closing stock → higher credit in Trading Account → higher Gross Profit (by ₹5,000) → higher Net Profit → higher Capital. Simultaneously, Balance Sheet shows Closing Stock at inflated value → Current Assets overstated by ₹5,000. A student who says "only profit is affected" misses the dual-effect principle: every adjustment hits both Profit & Loss and Balance Sheet. This tests understanding of the accounting equation linkage.

questions.q: Create a new adjustment scenario: A business has closing stock of ₹50,000 (cost) but market value is ₹45,000. The accountant records it at ₹50,000. Write the adjustment entry passed, the correct entry that should have been passed, and the impact on Gross Profit and Current Assets.
questions.a: Passed (wrong): Closing Stock A/c Dr. 50,000 To Trading A/c 50,000. Correct: Closing Stock A/c Dr. 45,000 To Trading A/c 45,000. Impact: Gross Profit overstated by ₹5,000; Current Assets overstated by ₹5,000. A poor answer that only writes the entry without quantifying impact shows inability to trace the ripple effect through final accounts.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Closing Stock ______ the cost of unsold goods remaining in the business at the end of an accounting period.
Fill in the blank: On March 31st, you have ₹15,000 worth of ______ kaju katli and laddoos in your display cases.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to: (1) Pass the correct adjustment journal entry for closing stock when given as additional information outside the Trial Balance, (2) Show its dual treatment in the Trading Account (credit side) and Balance Sheet (asset side), and (3) Distinguish this from the adjusted purchases method where closing stock.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: On March 31st, you have ₹15,000 worth of unsold kaju katli and ______ in your display cases.
